sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Cache setup and purpose
sections.what: Sets up the cache for model-written driver names, reusing the same table and expiry rules as the wider synthesis cache, under the ll-driver prefix.
sections.why: Stated in the comment: a second identical run makes zero model calls.
sections.watch_out: The day length and prefix are fixed here, so changing them affects which old entries are still seen.

sections.name: RawNameOutput
sections.title: Saved raw model reply
sections.what: Describes the exact model reply that was rejected: a name, a rationale and the example ids. It is kept so a later, stricter check can re-judge it without a new model call.
sections.why: The comment says a changed validator can re-judge the cached output instead of paying for the cluster again.
sections.watch_out: A saved reply is only as trustworthy as the checker that judged it, so rechecks should use the current rules.

sections.name: DriverNameEntry, l1
sections.title: Three kinds of saved answers
sections.what: Defines the three things the cache can hold: an accepted name with its rationale, a rejection with an optional raw reply, or a no-direction marker for imperative style.
sections.why: The comments explain that all three are cached so repeat runs make no new model calls.
sections.watch_out: Older entries that lack the raw reply are treated as misses and asked again.

sections.name: rowId
sections.title: Building the database row id
sections.what: Adds a fixed prefix to a cache key to make the row id used in the database.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps these entries separate from other cached AI results stored in the same table.
sections.watch_out: Changing the prefix makes all existing saved entries unreachable.

sections.name: getCachedDriverNames
sections.title: Reading a saved driver name
sections.what: Looks for a saved name first in memory, then in the database, ignoring expired rows. It only returns an entry if it has a valid shape, and keeps a copy in memory for later calls.
sections.why: Likely reason: saves money and time by avoiding repeated model calls for the same cluster.
sections.watch_out: The memory copy never expires while the process runs, so a changed database row may not be seen until a restart.

sections.name: setCachedDriverNames
sections.title: Saving a driver name
sections.what: Stores an answer in memory and in the database, with an expiry set from configuration. If the database write fails, it logs a warning and keeps the memory copy, so the run still continues.
sections.why: The comment says a failed cache write must never fail the whole run.
sections.watch_out: A failed database write is only logged, so after a restart that answer will have to be asked for again.

summary: A cache that stores model-written driver names so a repeat run does not ask the model again.
purpose: Saves cost and time, and keeps names stable between identical runs.
why: Stated in the comment: a second identical run makes zero model calls.
how: Reuses the existing synthesis cache table and its expiry rules, under a separate prefix so driver names do not clash with other cached results. Two access functions, one to read and one to write, handle a fast in-memory copy and a longer-lived stored copy.
inputs: Cache keys built from the driver inputs, and the name results returned by the model.
outputs: Previously stored names when the key matches, or nothing when there is no valid entry.
risks: Stale names can be reused until they expire. Cache hits may hide changes to the naming rules if the key does not include them.
debug: If names do not change after a code change, clear or let expire the cache entries with the ll-driver prefix. If the model is not called on a fresh run, check the key and the expiry days.
